verdict.rationale: NVIDIA documents 1,440 GB of total GPU memory across 8 B200 GPUs in a single DGX node. It also markets LLM inference performance, so a 70B-class quantized model plainly fits for single-node inference. However, the only bandwidth figure given is the 14.4 TB/s NVLink switch aggregate, which is interconnect bandwidth, not per-GPU HBM memory bandwidth. Missing for 10: published per-GPU HBM memory bandwidth spec, explicit per-GPU VRAM figure, hands-on or independent evidence of running a 70B quantized model.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run a 70B-class quantized LLM on this GPU — published VRAM capacity and memory bandwidth that make local or single-node inference practical

citations.quote: 8 x NVIDIA B200 GPUs that provide 1,440 GB total GPU memory
2 x 5th generation NVLink switches that provide 14.4 TB/s aggregate bandwidth
DGX B200 can handle diverse workloads—including large language models, recommender systems, and chatbots
NVIDIA DGX B200 delivers 3X the training performance and 15X the inference performance of previous-generation systems.
